study_design: Randomized, placebo-controlled cancer prevention trial with four intervention arms
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial (SELECT) randomized 35,533 healthy men, >55 yr old (>50 yr if African American), with normal digital rectal exams and prostate specific antigens <4 ng/ml to 1) 200 μg/day l-selenomethionine, 2) 400 IU/day all-rac-alpha-tocopheryl acetate (vitamin E), 3) both supplements, or 4) placebo for 7 to 12 yr.
reason: The trial reports overall prostate cancer incidence only. No aggressive, high-grade, advanced, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint is analyzed in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In SELECT, prostate cancer incidence did not differ among the 4 arms: hazard ratios [99% confidence intervals (CIs)] for prostate cancer were 1.13 (99% CI = 0.95-1.35, P = 0.06; n = 473) for vitamin E, 1.04 (99% CI = 0.87-1.24, P = 0.62; n = 432) for selenium, and 1.05 (99% CI = 0.88-1.25, P = 0.52; n = 437) for selenium + vitamin E vs. 1.00 (n = 416) for placebo.
estimate_classifications.reason: The selenium estimate is for overall prostate cancer incidence. The abstract reports a 99% CI, while the supplied row contains different CI values, but this does not alter the endpoint classification.
